basis: Intellectual disability in 10/10 patients and delayed language development define a neurodevelopmental disorder.
CNS neoplasia is a defining susceptibility site; prostate has no axis. Susceptibility does not establish existing brain injury.
The named syndrome defines ocular, skeletal and renal abnormalities; no further phenotype evidence supports additional axes.
Craniosynostosis and skeletal dysplasia define it; cataract/microphthalmia, callosal agenesis and ventricular septal defect each occur in 30–79%.
Inflammation affects the choroid and retina; neither infectious nor autoimmune etiology is established for this umbrella diagnosis.
Postinfectious urethral scarring causes urinary obstruction; the residual stricture does not establish ongoing infection or autoimmunity.
Peripheral neuropathy, intellectual disability and deafness define it; persistent lower-limb amyotrophy occurs in 80–99%, with foot deformity in 30–79%.
Disease of peripheral nerves; underlying systemic causes and muscle weakness do not establish additional organ damage across the umbrella.
Tumor originates in the mediastinum, which has no dedicated axis; lung, airway, pleural or other covered-organ involvement is not established.
Defective sperm morphology and male infertility are purely reproductive; no endocrine dysfunction is established.
Defined as an inherited glycosylation disorder, an inborn metabolic defect; no organ-specific phenotype evidence supports further labels.
Autoimmune injury of the inner ear causes rapidly progressive sensorineural hearing loss.
Inflammation is localized to the glans penis, a reproductive site; the umbrella includes noninfectious causes and does not establish autoimmunity.
Squamous carcinoma originates in the nasal cavity, which belongs to the airway axis.
Renal magnesium/calcium wasting, nephrocalcinosis and progressive renal failure define it; severe ocular damage is subtype-specific, with no group frequency established.
Mixed central and peripheral neural tumors with cutaneous neurofibromas define it; Lisch nodules do not impair vision, and hearing-loss frequency is unspecified.
Renal cysts progressively destroy kidney tissue; liver cysts usually preserve function, while substantial hepatic fibrosis is mainly a recessive-subtype feature.
The concept specifically identifies central nervous system vertigo; the generic definition's inner-ear causes do not establish ear involvement.
Loss of visual function defines the disorder; neurologic causes occur in a subset and do not justify a neurologic label across the umbrella.
Glomerular dysfunction causes persistent proteinuria and hypoalbuminemia; immune mediation is not established across this heterogeneous steroid-resistant group.
Aniridia, intellectual disability and urinary/urethral anomalies define it; hearing abnormalities occur in 30–79%. Wilms tumor risk alone is not counted as renal damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment, parkinsonism and axonal neuropathy define it; persistent distal muscle atrophy occurs in 2/2 assessed patients.
Folate deficiency impairs marrow DNA synthesis and causes megaloblastic anemia; no independent endocrine or inborn metabolic disorder is established.
Inherited cardiomyopathy with myocardial fibrosis, ventricular dilatation, dyskinesia and ventricular arrhythmias.
Defined as a vascular bleeding disorder; mucosal hemorrhage does not establish intrinsic airway/GI damage, and no blood-cell or coagulation defect is specified.
